attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, given as his own view.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the source and keeps the 'don't think as yet' qualifier and the Gemini scope. The central capability claim (can't yet take in a full episode or follow Succession) rests on 'don't think', a low-confidence belief like 'I suspect'. Only the 'can do this a little, often hallucinate' part is stated firmly.

contract.note: The contract treats the hedged 'don't think' clause as a testable plain-reading observation, but plain reading applies only to firm language. It also adds its own thresholds for 'take in', 'often' and 'in real time' that the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: Google's own 2024 post says Gemini 1.5 can take hour-long video input (frames, no audio). It shows input capacity, not comprehension of a full episode. It is an older model and not independent.

HourVideo, an independent 2024 benchmark, finds Gemini 1.5 Pro far below human experts on long first-person videos. Different content, a multiple-choice format and an earlier model mean it cannot settle the TV-comprehension claim.
VideoHallucer (2024) finds Gemini 1.5 Pro prone to hallucination on adversarial yes/no video questions. It does not measure heavy fabrication on complete episodes by models available in April 2025.

Google's announcement shows Gemini 2.5 Pro was available before the post date, so tests of 1.5 alone don't capture what Gemini could do then. It is a company statement and says nothing about video comprehension.

reviews.rationale: The core claim, that Gemini can't yet take in a full Simpsons episode or follow Succession, is hedged with 'don't think', which is low-confidence language and not scored. The firm parts ('can do this a little', 'often hallucinate heavily') would be unresolved anyway. All the evidence concerns earlier models, different tasks or company statements, and none tests full episodes with April 2025 models.
